Subject: Intro + demo: Redwood Inference — cross-region scheduling

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the interest — excited to show FinLytics how Redwood can help with lower-latency, predictable LLM inference for production workloads. We have a couple folks who should join from the EU team (Lukas, solutions engineer) so I wanted to propose a few slots that try to balance US morning and EU afternoon windows. Please let me know which works or send a few alternatives from your side.

Proposed 45-min demo slots (all converted to ET/CEST):
- Tue Apr 20 — 9:00am ET / 15:00 CEST
- Wed Apr 21 — 8:30am ET / 14:30 CEST
- Thu Apr 22 — 10:00am ET / 16:00 CEST

We also include a short 15-min tech deep-dive option later the same day if you want Lukas to walk through deployment/ops. I attached a short deck and can send a calendar invite once we lock a time.

I know timezone/DST confusion can be annoying — we double-checked US/EU DST changes for April. If any of these still land poorly for you, tell me the best 60–90 minute window and we’ll adapt.

Thanks,

Thanks, Sarah — good constraints. Based on 8:00–10:30am ET for you and trying to avoid late EU evenings, here are two concrete options that should be a reasonable trade-off for both teams:

Option A (recommended):
- Thu Apr 22 — 9:00am ET / 15:00 CEST — 45 minutes (demo + Q&A)

Option B (alternate):
- Wed Apr 21 — 8:30am ET / 14:30 CEST — 60 minutes (demo + short tech deep-dive)

Both slots keep the EU team in the afternoon rather than late evening. Lukas — can you confirm availability for either (I CC’d you). Once we confirm I’ll send a calendar invite with a Meet link and attach the deck/ICS.

A note on DST: both the US and EU are on DST in April, so ET -> CEST conversions above assume ET = UTC-4 and CEST = UTC+2. Wanted to call that out so there’s no surprise if someone is in a different timezone.

Thanks,
Marissa
